questions.stem: Circulation returns after the cesarean, and the client starts to bleed from IV sites. Which orders should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Massive transfusion with plasma, platelets and cryoprecipitate
Tranexamic acid
Uterotonics for atony
Fibrinogen, platelets and coagulation tests often
Heparin to treat clotting
Hold all blood products until labs return

rationale.correct: Balanced products, TXA, uterotonics and frequent labs.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The partner is in the waiting room asking what is happening. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

Tell the partner everything will be fine
Avoid speaking to the partner until the client is stable

questions.stem: After the head delivers, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Feel for a cord around the neck
Slip a loose cord over the head
Let the shoulders deliver with the next contraction, guiding gently
Dry the newborn and place skin to skin

Document that the provider was late as the cause of any injury

caseStudies.title: Precipitous birth with the nurse alone

exhibits.title: Labor room
exhibits.body: A 29-year-old client (G4 P3) arrived at 8 cm. The provider is 20 minutes away. The client was calm with breathing but is now irritable, nauseated and shaking, and says, "I can't do this anymore." Minutes later the client says, "The baby is coming," and the head is crowning.

rows.label: Help
cells: Call light pressed; another nurse coming
